method.label: Find a period and rule out smaller ones

annotationRationale: The sine shift identity and cosine's evenness establish a period. Sine's range and zeros, together with the inputs where cosine equals 1, establish minimality.
sourceMethod: Follows the official shift-by-pi argument and its minimality proof, explicitly using sine's range to justify when the composition equals 1.

review.mathCheck: The sign change of sine and evenness of cosine establish period \(\pi\). Any positive period T must satisfy \(\cos(\sin T)=1\); the sine range forces \(\sin T=0\), hence \(T\geq\pi\). Choice B is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 7's shift-and-minimality argument. The candidate explicitly explains why cosine equals 1 only at sine input 0.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed sine/cosine properties and supporting reduction formula match the worked method. No material omission.
